newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey incentives seen boosting economy.
newsitem.headline: Turkey incentives seen boosting economy.

text.p: Turkey's recent move to support small and medium factories (KOBI) by introducing new incentives would boost the Turkish economy in coming years, a state bank general manager said.

Yenal Ansen, general manager of Halkbank which specialises in low-interest loans to artisans and KOBIs, said the decree defining loan limits to KOBIs and interest rates on them showed the government was intent on supporting KOBIs' activities.

"The decree which took effect on October 16, shows KOBIs are fundamentals of the Turkish economy as they play an important role in raising exports, increasing employment and quality in production," Ansen told Reuters in an interview.
There are more than 200,000 KOBIs in Turkey, half of which receive finances from Halkbank in their investments.

Ansen said Halkbank which supplied 124 trillion lira of loans to artisans and KOBIs in January-October 1996, targeted 140 trillion lira for this year and double this figure for 1997. Loans to KOBIs stood at around 50 trillion lira in 1995.

The bank, with 78 percent of its total loans channelled to artisans and KOBIs, named 1996 "the year of KOBIs" and speeded up fund allocation for them and introduced an information service to help increase efficiency in this sector.
"We see the return of low-interest credits we provide to KOBIs in the form of a production increase in this sector and new value added to the overall economy," Ansen said.

"If we think about making profit, then we cannot provide these low-interest loans. But without making loss, we will continue to support them as our loans return to the system through new machinery or a newly employed person," he added.
Ansen said they gave priority to the manufacturing industry which contributes directly to economic improvement.

The new government decree introduced upper loan limits for different provinces -- 25 billion lira at 20 percent annual interest rate per KOBI in underdeveloped provinces and 20 billion lira at 30 percent in developed regions.
The loan maturity will be three years for both regions.
Turkey's year-on year wholesale inflation stood at 82.8 percent in October.
According to the decree, the Treasury will separately channel five trillion lira to KOBIs as a first tranche, with the amount to be raised in line with future demand.
Ansen said he expected the Treasury's part to go much higher in the 1997 budget, currently being discussed in parliament.
